value: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Wastewater Management (2010). Evaluation of Energy Conservation Measures for Wastewater Treatment Facilities. EPA 832-R-10-005, September 2010. Washington, DC. https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2016-01/documents/p1008sbm.pdf

Targeted extraction for the effluent-treatment aeration archetypes. MUNICIPAL WWTP DATA used as a proxy for industrial effluent aeration; nothing in the report is industrial. Loaded (main): Table 5-2 manufacturer blower cost ranges per blower unit by size band (equipment only, installation excluded, no price year so 2010 publication year used) with motor hp bands; Table 5-3 nominal isentropic blower efficiency and turndown (load-range-min) by blower type (reprinted from Gass 2009); Table 5-5 Oneida NY blower-set equipment costs in 2003$ (reprinted from Greene and Ramer 2007). Measures: aeration control (automated DO 10-30% of energy cost, TVA 14-40%, case studies 12-33%), fine-bubble vs coarse/mechanical 25-75% of aeration energy (30-40% common), turbo and single-stage blower savings, case-study costs and paybacks. Other-values: aeration share 25-60% of plant energy, single-unit blower quotes, Oneida energy cost and NPV. Not loaded: pumping (Ch.3), UV disinfection and mixing (Ch.6), solids processing (Ch.7), Appendix A case-study detail, Table 5-1 flow and pressure ranges. Locators are the printed chapter-page numbers (e.g. p.5-3). Traps: Table 5-2 prints "$325k-$4504" (k dropped before footnote 4; read as 450k). The list of tables numbers two tables 5-3 and calls the Oneida table 5-4; this extraction uses the body numbering (5-3 efficiencies, 5-4 turbo manufacturers, 5-5 Oneida). Blower efficiencies are isentropic, not wire-to-air. No heating values involved (electric equipment). Mapping is low throughout: blower components and per-unit costs do not match the per-GJ aeration-duty scope of the archetypes.
